source_policy: Each assertion backed by source urls within record; no unsupported measurement import; historical flora not claimed as source for these nine

records.name: Forestiera angustifolia
records.habit: Densely branched shrub or small tree; stiff lateral branchlets commonly branch nearly at right angles, elbow-like
records.leaves: Small narrow linear leaves in clusters along twigs; foliage variably semi-evergreen depending on region
records.flowers: Inconspicuous separate male/female flowers on separate plants; early spring clusters before leaves
records.habitat: Dry open sites, sandy well-drained soils and brush habitats
records.phenology: Flowers usually January–April across referenced Texas sites
records.taxonomic_note: Older names Forestiera puberula and F. texana reported by NPSOT; synonym status requires POWO check; do not conflate F. pubescens

records.name: Fraxinus berlandieriana
records.habit: Deciduous medium-sized tree to about 40 ft (12 m); broad dense rounded crown, drooping branches; trunk sometimes 2 ft (0.6 m) across
records.leaves: Opposite, odd-pinnately compound leaves 6–10 in long, commonly five lanceolate leaflets, occasionally three or seven; leaflets 3–4 in, remotely toothed at least distally
records.flowers: Dioecious; darker clustered male flowers often appear before leafout, loose female clusters with emerging leaves
records.fruit: Tan slender samaras 1–1.5 in long, about 0.25 in wide
records.bark: Gray to tan with narrow interwoven furrows/ridges
records.habitat: Stream and river margins in South Texas; extensively planted elsewhere
records.taxonomic_note: Do not merge with F. pennsylvanica, historically problematic in ash complexes

records.name: Fraxinus greggii
records.habit: Small shrub-like, nearly evergreen tree commonly to 16–20 ft (5–6 m)
records.leaves: Fine-textured dark-green pinnate foliage, individual compound leaves ca. 2 in long, lanceolate leaflets and fine marginal teeth according to University of Arizona arboretum
records.flowers: Small petal-less clustered flowers in spring; typically dioecious
records.habitat: Rocky limestone slopes, dry creek washes and canyons of southwest Texas and nearby Southwest
records.taxonomic_note: University source does not provide reliable samara dimensions; hold fruit measurements

records.name: Leucophyllum frutescens
records.habit: Dense, perennial evergreen shrub typically 2–5 ft (0.6–1.5 m), occasionally about 10 ft (3 m)
records.leaves: Simple elliptic to obovate blades mostly <=1 in (~2.5 cm), up to 1.25 in (~3.2 cm), entire and rounded apically, narrowed basally, dense silvery stellate pubescence
records.flowers: Crowded solitary axillary, approximately bell-shaped violet/purple/pink-lavender corollas up to 1 in in diameter and length
records.habitat: Rocky, well-drained limestone slopes, dry ravines and hillsides
records.phenology: Intermittent flowering spring through fall, often after rains; local season variable

records.name: Penstemon baccharifolius
records.habit: Woody-based or almost shrubby perennial often about 1–1.5 ft tall, sometimes to 20 in (50 cm)
records.leaves: Dark-green, somewhat thick, toothed blades, varying in hairiness
records.flowers: Cherry-red tubular flowers in clustered spikes on upper stems; attract hummingbirds
records.habitat: Limestone crevices, bluffs and rocky slopes of central/west Texas
records.phenology: April through October listed by wildflower center; flowering sporadic within range

records.name: Penstemon tenuis
records.habit: Rounded perennial herb, about 2–3 ft (0.6–0.9 m) including inflorescence
records.leaves: Opposite, broadly obovate, entire or toothed margins
records.flowers: Panicles with tubular pink, lavender or sometimes reddish corollas
records.habitat: Listed on dry rocky sites, crevices and bluffs by Texas Tech plant database; other habitats may differ
records.taxonomic_note: Flowering and site preferences vary among sources; compare FNA treatment rather than treating horticultural summaries as a species-wide range

records.name: Physostegia correllii
records.habit: Rhizomatous perennial herb often about 3 ft (~0.9 m) or taller, stout upright flowering stems
records.leaves: Dark-green sessile leaves with toothed margins, widest near middle; stems may have dark purplish-red coloration when young
records.flowers: Dense terminal spikes of tubular purple-pink speckled flowers during summer
records.habitat: Wet riparian stream and river margins, near water, sometimes in ditches and disturbed alluvial substrates
records.taxonomy: Rare conservation concern; do not map or disclose sensitive occurrence coordinates; no comparison with P. virginiana leaf widths without direct quantitative treatment

records.name: Salvia ballotiflora
records.habit: Aromatic perennial branching shrub about 3–5 ft (0.9–1.5 m), square stems; deciduous depending on winter
records.leaves: Small aromatic hairy oval serrated blades
records.habitat: Rocky sandy or gravelly brush slopes and well-drained limestone or calcareous soils
records.phenology: April–July according to Native Plant Society of Texas

records.name: Salvia pentstemonoides
records.habit: Large herbaceous perennial from persistent rootstocks, basal rosette and 1–several square flowering stalks to 5 ft (~1.5 m)
records.leaves: Smooth thick dark-green basal leaves to about 5 in (~12 cm)
records.flowers: Crimson/reddish-purple tubular flowers ca. 1.5 in (~4 cm); calyx initially green, becomes purple
records.habitat: Shaded limestone canyons, seeps, streamside bluffs and ledges in Edwards Plateau
records.phenology: Opportunistic blooming May–Nov depending on rainfall and soil moisture
records.taxonomy: IMPORTANT SPELLING: USFWS identifies pentstemonoides (extra t) as correct and penstemonoides as a frequent misspelling; retain repo slug salvia-pentstemonoides, not a different species
